newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher but off intraday highs.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher but off intraday highs.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher but below their intraday highs on late spillover weakness from CBOT corn, traders said.
"Corn broke and it kind of took the luster off wheat," a KCBT trader said.
Wheat had climbed higher at the midsession on short covering tied to ideas the market had become oversold. Commercial buying also helped support KCBT wheat.
"The market was overdue for a short-covering bounce, but I don't think anybody's convinced that the seasonal lows are in place," the same trader said.

KCBT wheat settled 2-1/2 to 5-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 5-1/2 cents at $3.23. Earlier, July had been as high as $3.25. September gained 4-1/4 cents to close at $3.29-1/2, but that was below the intraday high of $3.32.
Wheat also drew strength as showers slowed harvesting in parts of central Kansas and Oklahoma.
Benson-Quinn Commodities, a unit of ADM, bought 1.5 million December and two million March bushels. Cargill Investor Services bought 1.8 million Sept and General Mills bought 1.2 million Sept.
Featured sellers included Farmers Commodities, which shed two million Sept. Benson-Quinn sold 1.5 million Dec and 1.5 million Sept.
Traders said volume was moderate to heavy. The KCBT estimated Tuesday's wheat futures volume at 55.480 million bushels.
